commit.message:
fix(sim): fixture laws judge the whole stack over its true z span

Law (d2) swept only the flute disc along an upright rapid, so the
shank, holder and spindle housing could hit a clamp unreported. Law
(c2) stood every band at the move's deepest z, so on a ramp or plunge
the top of the stack at the high end was never judged.

A new verify::stack_span module gives both laws one span rule: each
piece of the tip path (a straight move, or an arc's 3-D chords) spans
[min(floor, piece low), piece high] in z, and a band above..above+len
is judged over [z_lo + above, z_hi + above + len] with the existing
strict band_hits_box. The window only ever grows over the old one, so
level moves keep their verdicts sum for sum, and the strict-dip
silences (a retract off a mounting face, flush contact) hold for the
whole stack. An upright rapid keeps its disc verdict (Rapid) first,
then names the shank, holder or spindle struck, then the flute column
above the tip (Rapid). A non-finite z now fails closed.

Pinned by sim fixture_stack_span (7) and app fixture_law_gaps (3):
the #424 retract and traverse repros, the #425 ramp repro, a helical
ramp, and post-gate refusals by name for a face program's retract and
plunge.

Fixes #424
Fixes #425

Merge remote-tracking branch 'upstream/main' (#381 HolderStack) into issue/424-425-fixture-law-gaps

#381 landed: the bands law and the posed sweep read a HolderStack. The
#424 upright-rapid stack (stack_span::upper_bands) now takes that same
HolderStack - shank, the holder's own bands, the housing on holder.top
- instead of the tool's holder cylinder, so an upright rapid judges a
modelled holder body. Pinned by
fixture_stack_span::an_upright_rapid_reads_a_modelled_holder_bodys_bands
(a slim r5 cylinder clears the bolt; the body's r20 collar must hit).
